items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1959-08-20
items.q: So I come on and join Jack Carey. And I played with Jack a long climb, man.

ctx.x: Yeah, Dave Bailey. Yeah, well that's Ernest Johnson's brother. See? They must be half brother. But anyhow, they were always there, we were out in front of town there on Chippy Ward in St. Thomas. That's where they lived then. And what made me go out there, it was a boy out in the army, what he did now, I forget his name, but his mother lived out there and he told me to come and I could stay with him. That's how we were good friends in the army see? So he brought me there and they really treated me nice. I lived…
Well nobody's found it yet. I've heard talk of his record. He's supposed to have made, but you never know.

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1957-multiple
items.q: I worked with Carey, Carey just about three years.

ctx.x: Well, to tell the truth, he played with me in my band. I had a band. He worked with me. Then a couple of times he worked with Jack Carey. Who?
What was he playing in those days?

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1959-09-25
items.q: That's how I got with his brother Jack Carey.

ctx.x: No. I just thought maybe you knew some of the different guys that worked with him. No,

see he always worked at Spanish Food, that's where he always worked. And we never did go out there, we went to Millenburg, pretty like that, but I never did go to Spanish Food. I don't know, you don't even know the place where he worked at out there. Did you ever work with B-Rod? Yeah. How'd that happen? You mean, playing in the band with him? Well no, we made records on one side, he made them on the other side, but we were always in the same building, in New York, when I made it in Mexico with Edwin Hall. Yeah.…
Met him in New York or in California? No, New York. I see. Did you ever know Richard M Jones?
